Architecture Diagram

The solution is a single ASP.NET Web Forms catalog application. It serves server-rendered pages and accesses catalog data through an application service backed by Entity Framework 6 or, when configured, an in-memory mock service.

Data Storage & External Services

The application uses a SQL Server LocalDB connection configured for integrated security. Entity Framework owns catalog persistence; startup seed data can be selected from built-in data or local CSV files. Application Insights web tracking is configured, but no instrumentation key or explicit remote endpoint is present in the checked-in configuration. There is no cache or message broker.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • ICatalogService separates Web Forms pages from persistence and provides a mock implementation.
  • Autofac selects a singleton mock service when UseMockData is true, and a per-lifetime-scope EF service otherwise.
  • EF6 uses a custom high/low sequence generator for catalog identifiers and a database initializer for schema setup and seed data.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType are domain/data model classes used by the page controls and service layer. PaginatedItemsViewModel packages page metadata and the current item sequence. These are mutable classes, not immutable records. The application renders HTML through Web Forms and does not declare an OpenAPI specification, protobuf schema, GraphQL schema, or JSON API contract.

Communication Patterns

Page handlers call ICatalogService synchronously in-process. With UseMockData=true, Autofac selects the mock service; otherwise, CatalogService uses EF6 for synchronous database calls. No message broker, service discovery, API gateway, retry, timeout, circuit-breaker, or client-side load-balancing implementation was found. Application-level authentication and authorization are not configured in the inspected Web.config; transport TLS is left to the IIS hosting configuration and is not specified in this project.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports catalog browsing and basic catalog administration for an e-commerce storefront. Its primary business objects are products, brands, and product types.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalogProduct sold or displayed in the storefrontBelongs to one CatalogBrand and one CatalogType
CatalogBrandCatalogProduct brand classificationCan classify multiple CatalogItems
CatalogTypeCatalogProduct type/category classificationCan categorize multiple CatalogItems

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopLegacyWebFormsCatalogCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server LocalDB in database mode; none for in-memory mock mode

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse Catalog

  1. A visitor requests the default catalog page or a paginated route.
  2. The page uses supplied route values or the default page size/index.
  3. ICatalogService.GetCatalogItemsPaginated returns an ordered item page with its brand/type details and total count.
  4. The page binds the items and builds previous/next navigation links.
  5. The server returns rendered HTML.

Workflow 2: Maintain a Catalog Item

  1. A catalog editor opens Create or Edit and enters product information.
  2. The page checks its model state and constructs a CatalogItem.
  3. The catalog service assigns an identifier for new items or updates the existing EF entity, then saves changes.
  4. The user is redirected to the catalog page.

Workflow 3: Delete a Catalog Item

  1. The page resolves an item by route ID and displays its details.
  2. On the delete postback, the service removes the selected item.
  3. The user is redirected to the catalog page.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No independently deployed services or cross-service data aggregation were identified. The page layer calls one catalog service; database mode persists with EF6, while mock mode operates on an in-memory list.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Visitor participant Page as "Default catalog page" participant Service as "Catalog service" participant DB as "Catalog database" Visitor->>Page: Browse catalog Page->>Page: Resolve page number and size Page->>Service: Request catalog page Service->>DB: Load catalog items with brand and type DB-->>Service: Catalog data and total count Service-->>Page: Paginated catalog view Page->>Page: Bind items and navigation Page-->>Visitor: Rendered catalog page

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog item prices are constrained to non-negative values with at most two fractional digits by the model validation attributes.
  • Stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock values have non-negative range limits up to ten million.
  • EF mapping requires a name (maximum 50 characters), price, picture filename, brand, and type; brand and type text fields are required and limited to 100 characters.
  • New catalog item identifiers are supplied by a high/low SQL sequence in database mode or by incrementing the current maximum ID in mock mode.
  • UseMockData selects the service implementation; UseCustomizationData selects built-in versus CSV/image seed content.
  • No explicit transaction orchestration beyond EF SaveChanges, audit trail, or application-level authorization rules were identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses legacy packages.config package management. Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.1 is affected by high-severity CVE-2024-21907; the advisory’s patched version is 13.0.1. The AppCAT upgrade assessment also reports incompatible or upgrade-recommended NuGet packages for a net10.0 target. A dependency-tree command could not evaluate transitive packages because Microsoft.WebApplication.targets is missing from the assessment runner.

Notable Observations

  • The framework dependency is ASP.NET Web Forms/System.Web, which is not part of modern .NET.
  • The checked-in package set includes separate Application Insights collectors and web packages.
  • Microsoft.Net.Compilers is marked as a development dependency in packages.config.
  • No test-scoped NuGet dependencies were declared.

Caching Strategy

No dedicated caching provider or cache policy is configured. When UseMockData is true, CatalogServiceMock holds a mutable preconfigured list in memory; this is application state rather than a configured cache. In database mode, data is queried from EF6 without an explicit result cache.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The single web application is the source of truth for catalog items, brands, and types. All tables reside in the same configured database; no cross-service reads, aggregation, CQRS, or event-based data exchange was identified. Web Forms pages call the catalog service, which owns normal EF6 reads and writes; the initializer separately performs database setup and seed operations.
